name: Native text field
summary: A native text field for typing (system keyboard: spaces, numbers, punctuation, autocorrect, dictation), with the submitted text recorded in the replay log. The engine has it (input sources {"text": "submit"} and {"text": "change"}, presentation.text_field, replay and verify record the text); the app runtime (bubble-kit-microgame.js) and the JS playtest bots don't drive it yet, so games type on the keyboard fragment grid.
when_to_use: Plan for it in typed games (typed_answer, qa_bank, fill-in, name-the-thing), but compose with the keyboard fragment until it ships: the phone shows no field for a text source today, and the bots never type, so a game that only takes text fails the gate.
api: inputs.<name>.from: [{"text": "submit" | "change", "placeholder"?: string, "max_len"?: int <= 200}] with record text {value: string}; presentation.text_field {x, y, w, h, size}; the field clears after submit; engine JS: game.text("submit" | "change", value); replay log line {"t": ms, "text": "submit", "value": "..."}
gaps_it_closes: typing only through the keyboard fragment grid
no spaces, digits, punctuation or autocorrect in typed answers
notes: engine side done (SPEC-v0.2 section 4, mg-cli sim types random text). Needed: Artem, the field in bubble-kit-microgame.js; Bayan, bots that type (a playtest.texts list). Request text in docs/harness-gaps/open-text.md

name: Answer bank
summary: Server-side content step: for each prompt, the accepted answers with aliases and also_accept lists, written by Muse at build time and checked for duplicates and reach.
when_to_use: Open-answer games where many answers are right: name a…, list games, rare-answer trivia.
api: answer_bank(prompts[], {theme, per_prompt}) -> [{prompt, answers: [{text, aliases[], also_accept[]}]}]

name: Rarity tiers
summary: Sorts each prompt's accepted answers into tiers (common, uncommon, rare, legendary) by how often people would give them, so rarer answers can score more.
when_to_use: Rare-answer trivia and any typed game that rewards obscure answers; feeds typed_answer's tier string.
api: rarity_tiers(answer_bank) -> per prompt "a,b,c|d,e|f|g" (most common tier first)

name: Question bank
summary: Server-side content step: themed questions with a difficulty rating, the right answer and plausible distractors, checked for one right answer and no repeats.
when_to_use: Quizzes and trivia that should ramp in difficulty or draw from a large themed pool.
api: question_bank({theme, count, difficulty: [lo, hi], choices}) -> [{q, answer, distractors[], difficulty}]

name: Level list
summary: Server-side content step: an ordered list of levels or puzzle boards for one mechanic, each checked solvable by a solver or bot, with rising difficulty.
when_to_use: Puzzle and platform games played as a sequence of hand-made-feeling levels.
api: level_list({type_id, count, difficulty_curve}) -> [{level, data, solution?, difficulty}]

name: Themed word list
summary: Server-side content step: a themed word list with lengths and filters (only dictionary words, a fixed length, no proper nouns), for word games.
when_to_use: Hidden-word guessing, word search, hangman-like and spelling games with a theme.
api: word_list({theme, count, length?, dictionary_only?}) -> [string]

name: Web lookup
summary: When the catalog misses a named game, looks it up on Wikipedia and the named site, and has Muse write a candidate game_type (mechanic only, with source URLs), saved as learned.
when_to_use: A request names a game, site or format the catalog has no alias for, or retrieval scores are low.
api: lookup(name) -> {game_type (status learned), refs[]}; budget 8 s; on failure the job continues without it

name: Friend answers
aliases: how well do you know me
summary: Collects short answers or picks from specific friends or a Group (about themselves or each other) so a game can ask players to guess them.
when_to_use: Guess-your-friends and party games whose content is the players themselves.
api: POST answers per game and person; GET a game's collected answers for players
notes: needs a backend endpoint; not in backend/README.md yet

name: Async turns
summary: Turn-based play between friends on their own phones, move by move: the server stores the game state and whose move it is, and tells the next player. Unlike group play, the players share one board.
when_to_use: Board, word and strategy games where each move depends on the other player's last move (a correspondence match). Most games don't need it: same-seed rounds (chat_round) compare separate runs.
api: planned: POST /v1/matches {gameId, players[]}; POST /v1/matches/{id}/moves {move, log}; GET /v1/matches/{id} -> {state, turn, moves}
notes: Needs Max (match store) and Artem (a game that resumes from a stored state and a move list, replay-verified move by move). Until then, approximate with the turns fragment on one phone, or a same-seed round.

name: Freehand drawing
summary: Captures a finger-drawn stroke as points the game can keep, show and score. Can be approximated today with pointer move input plus a poly node (256 points); there is no stroke recognition.
when_to_use: Drawing and tracing games, draw-a-path puzzles, doodle guessing.
api: approximation: inputs from {"pointer": "move"} pushing points to state; poly {points}

name: Share grid
summary: A spoiler-free result grid (rows of coloured squares) a player can share after a run. Microgames share score text only today.
when_to_use: Daily puzzles and word games whose result people post to compare.

name: Segment collision
summary: Collision against line segments and polylines (walls, ropes, laser beams, drawn lines). Physics and helpers cover circles and unrotated boxes only.
when_to_use: Bouncing off drawn lines, mazes with thin walls, lasers, slicing.

name: Joints and constraints
summary: Physics joints: ropes, hinges, springs and chains between bodies.
when_to_use: Swinging, rope cutting, ragdolls, bridges, cranes.

name: Rotated collision shapes
summary: Bodies that rotate and collide as rotated boxes or polygons, with angular velocity. Images can be drawn rotated, but physics and overlap tests are axis-aligned.
when_to_use: Stacking that topples, tumbling blocks, angled platforms, spinning obstacles.

name: Device sensors (tilt)
summary: Tilt, motion and shake from the phone's sensors as game inputs.
when_to_use: Tilt to roll a ball, tilt to steer, shake to roll dice.
notes: approximate tilt with player_drag or hold_buttons

name: Live multiplayer
summary: Two or more people playing the same game at the same time on their own phones.
when_to_use: Live duels, races and party games across phones.
notes: approximate with turns (one phone), ghost_score or score_challenge (async)

name: 3D
summary: Three-dimensional scenes and cameras. The engine is 2D only.
when_to_use: Requests that need real 3D; usually re-planned as top-down, side-on or layered 2D.
notes: the anatomy prompt names this gap "3d"; catalog ids must start with a letter

name: Voice input
summary: Spoken answers transcribed into the game as text input.
when_to_use: Say-the-answer trivia, singing or shouting games, accessibility.
notes: Muse has a transcription model (muse-voice-transcribe-1.0); nothing in the runtime records audio

name: Multi-touch
summary: More than one finger at a time. The engine tracks one pointer: a second press releases the first.
when_to_use: Two-thumb controls, two players on one screen at once, pinch gestures.
notes: approximate with alternating turns or one-thumb controls

name: Layered loop player
summary: Plays several sound loops at once, in sync, each with its own on/off and volume, so players can layer and mix them.
when_to_use: Ambient mixers, loop stations, layered band and beat games.
gaps_it_closes: only one music loop plays at a time
notes: today presentation.music loops one rendered WAV, and timers can retrigger synth notes as step loops (see step_grid)

name: Sound clip content
summary: Recorded or sampled sound clips as content (animal calls, real instruments, spoken words, everyday sound effects) from a licensed or CC0 sound library, for listen-and-answer games.
when_to_use: Name-that-sound and guess-the-sound-effect games that need real recordings. For music, use melody_clip (original tunes, shipped).
notes: Original synth melodies ship as melody_clip. Real songs and recordings can't be copied into games; a library must be CC0 or licensed with the source recorded. Kevin's sound-library idea (Slack, 22:29) belongs to Artem and Max; see docs/harness-gaps/audio.md, Requests.
api: planned, compatible with melody_clip: sound.clips entries may be {library: "<sound id>"} next to note clips; the server resolves the id to a URL or data URI and the asset is still clip_<i>, so play_clip and feedback {sound: {asset}} work unchanged

name: Real-time growth
summary: Game state that persists between runs and advances with real time, so a plant, pet or garden grows between daily visits.
when_to_use: Daily care, idle growth, shared gardens and streaks that last days.
gaps_it_closes: game state resets every run; nothing carries over between days
notes: needs per-player (or per-Group) saved state on the backend; saves today are likes. shared_progress carries only a Group's total score

name: Collection book
summary: A collection that fills across runs (fish caught, stickers found), shown as a book with blanks for what's missing.
when_to_use: Fishing, collecting and gacha-like cozy games.
notes: within one run it's plain list state; across runs it needs the same saved state as growth_timer

name: Spaced repetition
summary: Schedules each card's next review by how well it was remembered, across days.
when_to_use: Study and vocabulary games played daily.
notes: needs saved per-player state (see growth_timer)

name: Drag to reshape
summary: Dragging changes a surface under the finger: wiping fog, raking sand, shaping clay.
when_to_use: Calm tactile toys: wipe the window, rake the sand, shape the pot.
notes: approximate with a coarse grid() of values changed by pointer move and drawn as rects; fine detail needs a real surface

name: Shape match score
summary: Scores how close a drawn stroke is to a target shape (average distance between the stroke and target points).
when_to_use: Tracing, draw-from-memory, perfect-circle and calligraphy games.
api: planned: shape_score(stroke: list<vec2>, target: list<vec2>) -> 0..1
notes: can be approximated in rules with map, min_of and dist over the points, within collection limits

name: Colour mixer
summary: Mixes amounts of base colours into a resulting colour and measures how close it is to a target swatch.
when_to_use: Colour matching and mixing puzzles.
gaps_it_closes: no builtin turns numbers into a colour string
notes: the mix is plain maths, but the result must become a '#RRGGBB' string; a hex digit lookup list in rules works around it

name: Fill a region
summary: Tap a closed region of a line drawing to fill it with the current colour.
when_to_use: Colouring books and colour-by-number with real pictures.
notes: works today when regions are grid_board cells (pixel_grid); free-form regions need region shapes as content plus poly fills

name: Toppling stack physics
summary: Pieces stack and can tip over: physics with rotation, so off-centre weight topples the stack.
when_to_use: Balance and stacking games where toppling is the drama.
notes: physics_world stacks unrotated boxes and circles (no tipping); the gold slice_drop_stacker and pass_play_stacker fake it with overhang rules

name: Map pin guess
aliases: where in the world is it
summary: Shows a clue, the player pins a guess on a real map, and the score falls with the great-circle distance from the true place.
when_to_use: Where-was-this-taken, pin-the-capital, find-the-country and place quizzes. Compose it from geo_map + map_pin + rounds + lives with a `geo` section (target: capital or label).
notes: Example game Pin the Capital passes the gate and the score check. Needs the manifest's `geo` section, which expander/geo.mjs turns into the map sprite, the geo_* functions and the rect and projection params. Example games pass the gate (authoring/content/geo/examples, built by tools/make-geo-games.mjs). Status building until the Studio pipeline calls applyGeo before expand and the bundle carries the packs and fragments (request in docs/harness-gaps/maps.md). Photos for where-was-this-taken are a separate gap (photo_picker, image_gallery).
api: composed: uses geo_map, map_pin, rounds (round_done = pin_done), lives (hit = pin_far), score; game functions map_target() = get_or(geo_target(), current, vec(0.0, 0.0)), map_can_pin(), map_focus() = if pin_shown then current else -1; rule on pinned: incr score by pin_points(event.km)

name: Geography content pack
summary: Checked place data built at build time from Natural Earth (public domain): 177 countries and the 51 US states and DC with simplified outlines, label points, bounding boxes, continent and subregion, capitals with coordinates, and aliases. A game names places; coordinates and outlines come only from the pack.
when_to_use: Any geography game: the `geo` section picks or names places from a pack, and the geo step writes their names, capitals, coordinates and outlines into the game.
notes: Built by tools/make-geo-pack.mjs from ne_110m_admin_0_countries, ne_110m_populated_places_simple and ne_110m_admin_1_states_provinces (v5). world.json 147 KB, us_states.json 25 KB; a game carries only its own places (10–30 KB with the map). No flags (Natural Earth has none; see the request) and no cities beyond capitals yet.
api: authoring/content/geo/<pack>.json (geo-pack/1); manifest `geo` {pack, places | pick {region, count, min_area, seed}, target: label|capital, map, outline, quiz {choices, ask: name|capital}}; expander/geo.mjs applyGeo(manifest, packs); unknown places are A_GEO_PLACE errors

name: Meaning-closeness ranking
summary: For a secret word, a ranked list of other words by how close their meaning is, written at build time, so guesses can be told how warm they are.
when_to_use: Guess-the-word-by-meaning daily puzzles.
api: planned: content list ranked by closeness; in-game index_of(ranked, guess) gives the rank
gaps_it_closes: no embeddings (Muse has no embeddings endpoint)
notes: a Muse-written ranking covers only the words it lists; guesses outside it read as cold

name: Picture set
summary: A set of themed pictures as game content (scenes, objects, animals, places), one per round, as the frames of one picture sprite.
when_to_use: Picture puzzles, close-up guessing, picture trivia, jigsaws, frame-reveal guessing.
gaps_it_closes: art roles are sprites for pieces, not a list of full pictures per round
notes: SVG frames work today (zoom_reveal, picture_quiz). A raster sheet needs a build-time step that tiles generated or CC0 pictures into one JPEG under the 192 KB art budget (about 6 pictures at 384 px); requested from Max
api: art.sprites.picture = {svg: [one SVG per round], w: 512, h: 512} (works today); raster rounds = one image sheet {image: data URI, frames, cols} made at build time

name: In-game image generation
aliases: make a picture from my prompt
summary: Generates a picture from a player's prompt during play.
when_to_use: Prompt-the-picture and describe-and-draw games.
gaps_it_closes: art is made once at build time, not during play
notes: muse-image-1.0 exists (about 13-18 s, 1600-1920 px WebP, ~0.5 MB), but games run offline and deterministically; a live call breaks replays and needs a server round trip. Build-time pictures are generated_image

name: Image similarity
summary: Scores how similar two pictures are.
when_to_use: Match-the-picture games.
notes: no model or endpoint for it

name: Drawing recognizer
summary: Names what a drawing shows.
when_to_use: Draw-it-and-the-computer-guesses games.
notes: approximate with friends guessing (friend_pairing, vote_tally)

name: Written answer grader
summary: Grades a short written answer against key points with Muse after the run.
when_to_use: Explain-it-back and short-answer learning games.
gaps_it_closes: typed answers can only be matched, not judged
notes: a Muse call is not deterministic, so the grade must be stored with the run rather than replayed; fuzzy_match covers short answers

name: Track list
summary: A list of song titles and artists to choose from, for playlist and music-taste games (names only, no audio).
when_to_use: Playlist curating and music-taste voting.
notes: titles can come from web_lookup; choosing among them works with quiz or sort_bins

name: Text to speech
summary: Speaks a word or phrase aloud for the player to type or repeat.
when_to_use: Spelling bees, dictation and listening practice.
notes: Muse lists a transcription model but no speech model; the runtime only synthesizes tones

name: Microphone input
summary: Records sound from the microphone during a run.
when_to_use: Singing, humming, beatboxing and foley games.
notes: same gap as voice_input

name: Pitch detection
summary: Detects the pitch of a sung or played note from the microphone.
when_to_use: Sing-the-note and tuning games.
notes: needs mic_input first

name: Sound classifier
summary: Labels recorded sounds (kick, snare, clap).
when_to_use: Beatbox and sound-sorting games.
notes: needs mic_input first

name: Speech input
summary: Turns what the player says into text for checking.
when_to_use: Pronunciation and say-the-answer games.
notes: same gap as voice_input; muse-voice-transcribe-1.0 could do the server side

name: Song generation
summary: Composes a song with lyrics and style from a description.
when_to_use: Make-a-song creative games.
notes: games can compose synth melodies from notes (note_grid, audio_synth); there is no vocal or full-song generation

name: Video scene
summary: Plays a short video in the game.
when_to_use: Foley, dubbing and react-to-a-clip games.
notes: approximate with an animated sprite scene (image_assets frames)

name: Tilt input
summary: Phone tilt or shake as input.
when_to_use: Tilt to roll, shake to stir.
notes: same gap as device_sensors; approximate with drag or swipe

name: Flashlight beam
summary: The scene is dark except a beam or circle of light the player moves; only what's inside it is visible.
when_to_use: Dark exploration, horror and hide-and-seek.
gaps_it_closes: no masking or clipping in rendering
notes: approximate: draw objects only when dist to the light is under the radius, over a dark background; a true mask with soft edges needs engine support

name: Limited light
summary: A light radius that shrinks as its fuel runs down and resets when refuelled; only things inside it are shown.
when_to_use: Light-rationing horror and survival exploration.
gaps_it_closes: no masking or clipping in rendering
notes: same approximation as flashlight_mask, with the radius from a timer_bar

name: Vision cone
summary: Guards see in a cone; the player is spotted when inside a guard's cone and range, unless cover blocks the view.
when_to_use: Stealth games and sneaking puzzles.
notes: the cone test works in rules (angle, dist, atan2) and a poly can draw it; blocking by cover needs segment_collision

name: Directional sound
aliases: where is the sound coming from
summary: Plays a sound so it seems to come from a direction (left, right, behind).
when_to_use: Locate-the-sound games and audio horror.
notes: synth sounds have wave, pitch, length and volume but no pan; approximate direction with pitch or volume cues

name: Anomaly variants
summary: Builds two versions of one scene: the scene as written, and a copy where N objects are recolored, removed, moved, resized or say something else, with each change's hitbox recorded. Deterministic from a seed.
when_to_use: Spot-the-difference, what-changed and find-the-anomaly rounds. Muse writes the scene (simple placed shapes, text and emoji); code makes the changes, so the answer key always matches the pictures.
api: authoring/expander/spot-diff.mjs: makeSpotDifference(scene {w, h, bg, objects: [{id, shape rect|circle|ellipse|text|poly|line, geometry, fill, fixed?, alt?}]}, {count 3..9, seed, kinds}) -> {a, b, diffs [{id, kind, x, y, r, box}], decoys, problems}; toAuthoring(result) -> {art.sprites picture_a/picture_b, functions diff_points/diff_radii/diff_decoys} for diff_spots. CLI: authoring/tools/make-diff-game.mjs
notes: SVG only: changes inside one generated raster picture are not possible (no inpainting); a raster pair would need Muse Image editing. The compose step does not call it yet: the planner needs a "scene" content slot and a call to toAuthoring (see docs/harness-gaps/images.md)

name: Yes/no fact bank
summary: Build-time content step for qa_bank games: Muse writes each case (setup, hidden solution), 30-60 facts with a yes/no/irrelevant/partly reply and the concept words players use, and the solutions; then plays it (40 probe questions with true replies), and repairs the facts the matcher gets wrong, once. Checked by checkBank (shape, every fact's own question lands on it, no stop-word groups).
when_to_use: Every qa_bank game: lateral puzzles, twenty questions, interrogations. One bank per case; a daily puzzle is one case per day.
api: bankPrompt({request, count, puzzle?}) -> qa-bank/1 {cases: [{title, setup, solution, facts: [{ask, reply, key, match: [[words]], also_ask}], solve: [[[words]]], hints}]}; probePrompt(case) -> {questions: [{q, reply}]}; probeFailures(case, questions); repairPrompt(bank, failures); toContent(bank) -> {qa_setups, qa_reveals, qa_facts, qa_solves} (authoring/expander/qa-bank.mjs); CLI authoring/tools/qa-bank-muse.mjs --refine
gaps_it_closes: no LLM at play time for free questions
notes: module and CLI built and measured (3 Muse calls, about 2 min, per case); not yet called by the generator's compose step, which would need a content-step hook in pipeline.mjs

name: Judged replies
summary: Build-time content step for npc_judge: per round, the character's line, 3-4 replies in the person's theme, a 0-100 rating of each in the character's voice (one clearly best, one flop) and the character's reaction to each.
when_to_use: Rizz, convince-the-bouncer, roast or debate judges, caption contests with a judge: any npc_judge game.
api: planned: npc_lines({theme, character, rounds, choices}) -> {lines[], options[], ratings[], reactions[]} flattened per round for nj_lines/nj_options/nj_ratings/nj_reactions; today compose writes these straight into content

name: Live AI answer while playing
summary: A server endpoint the game calls during play to have Muse answer a question or judge free text the bank doesn't cover; the answer is stored with the run and written into the replay log, so verification replays the recorded answer instead of calling Muse again.
when_to_use: Not available. Plan typed-judging ideas (rate my own pickup line, free chat with a character, judge my caption) as npc_judge with written replies, or qa_bank with an "Ask another way" miss, and say in the plan that live judging is a gap.
api: proposed: POST /v1/games/{id}/ask {run_id, seq, text} -> {reply, label?, rating?} (Muse Spark at minimal effort, 5-12 s); the engine receives it as an input event {"ask_reply": {seq, reply}} logged like any input; verify replays the log; per-user rate limits and a moderation pass
gaps_it_closes: questions or text outside the build-time bank
notes: needs Max (endpoint, cost, abuse limits) and Artem (an async host input that the runtime injects and the replay log records); 5-20 s per Muse call is too slow per turn for most games. See docs/harness-gaps/open-text.md

name: Pictures made at build time
summary: While a game is being made, the server asks muse-image-1.0 for each picture the plan needs (an animal, a scene, a cartoon character), shrinks it, and stores it with the game, so every player sees the same pictures and replays verify.
when_to_use: Picture rounds that need more than flat SVG can draw: wildlife or nature close-ups, painterly scenes, cartoon caricatures of generic characters. Never photos or likenesses of real people: a real person in the request becomes a generic cartoon character, and the plan says so.
api: planned: plan.content.pictures = [{id, prompt, style}] -> server returns {id, src (data URI or games-host URL), w, h, license: "generated"}; the expander puts them in one sprite sheet (image_gallery)
gaps_it_closes: games can only show pictures Muse can draw as SVG
notes: tested 2026-11-12 from the Mac: 2 calls, 13.3 s and 17.7 s, 1920x1280 and 1600x1600 WebP (538 KB and 620 KB; the size parameter was ignored), photo-real quality; a 384 px JPEG is 32-43 KB. Needs Max (generation in the job, storage) and Bayan (style consistency); see docs/harness-gaps/images.md

name: Public-domain picture packs
summary: Curated packs of real photos under CC0 or public-domain terms (for example Wikimedia Commons or iNaturalist CC0 observations), each with its source URL, author and license recorded, pre-shrunk for games.
when_to_use: When the request wants real photos rather than generated ones: wildlife photo trivia, landmarks, food close-ups. Never photos of people.
api: planned: packs/<topic>.json [{answer, aliases, src, w, h, source_url, author, license}] on the games host; the plan picks a pack and N entries by seed
gaps_it_closes: no real photos with a known license
notes: needs a one-time curation pass and storage on Max's games host; generated_image is the faster path for the demo

name: Clipped image window
summary: Draw part of an image: a group that clips its children to its box, or an image node with a source rectangle, so a picture can zoom or pan inside a window without covering the screen around it.
when_to_use: Zoom-out reveals over a backdrop, magnifier and spotlight effects, sliding-window pictures, jigsaw pieces cut from one picture.
api: requested from Artem: group prop clip: true (clip children to the group box), or image props src_x, src_y, src_w, src_h (fractions of the frame)
gaps_it_closes: zoom_reveal masks with $bg rects, hiding the backdrop around its window
notes: the renderer already clips the whole frame (render.js drawFrame); a per-group clip is a save/clip/restore around the subtree
